neighbours.label: talk of a society or group being divided or polarized, peaking on the word that names the fault line (split along racial lines, the social divide); output promotes ' divide'/' along'
fire: The referendum split the country along regional and linguistic lines.
Analysts warn that the debate is widening the partisan divide in Congress.
The town has long been segregated along racial and religious lines.
Voters remain sharply polarized over immigration and taxes.
Leaders hope the new coalition can bridge the deep sectarian rift.
The strike divided the workforce into two bitterly opposed factions.
The election exposed a growing urban-rural divide among voters.
Critics accused the party of pitting citizens against each other on the basis of class.
quiet: The referendum was held in the country on a sunny Sunday in June.
Analysts warn that the debate is running late in Congress tonight.
The town has long been known for its bakeries and religious festivals.
Voters remain sharply focused on the price of bread and fuel.
Leaders hope the new bridge can carry traffic across the deep river.
The strike lasted two weeks before the workforce returned to the factory.
The election brought a record turnout among young voters.
Critics accused the party of spending too much on the new stadium.

notes: card: peaks on ' along' (fracture along lines), ' bridge' (polarised landscape), ' social' (divide), segregate ' on' the basis of race; the + pole suppresses divide/faction/sectarian. Probe: 'fractured the party along ideological lines' 0.99, physical 'river divides the farm' 0.04.
